title: Align textures on surfaces
summary: Shift, repeat, rotate, skew, fit, or reset a selected brush face's projection.
outcome: Texture placement follows the intended face and scale.

sections.title: Edit the projection

steps.title: Select faces
steps.text: Switch to Face mode (S), click a brush face in Camera, and Shift-click any additional faces. A whole brush selection can also expose its surfaces in the inspector.

steps.title: Enter alignment
steps.text: In Texture alignment, set horizontal and vertical shift, repeat size, rotation, and skew, then click Apply. Shift and repeat size use world units; negative repeat sizes mirror the texture.

steps.title: Fit or reset
steps.text: Set horizontal and vertical repeat counts and click Fit to align each selected face. Axial resets shift, rotation, and skew to axis-aligned mapping while retaining repeat sizes. Revert restores the inspector draft without editing the map.

paragraphs: Modify > Texture projection provides quick horizontal flip, vertical flip, and 90° rotation of selected texture projections.
tips: Apply alignment fields before Fit if Fit should use those new values. If the projection fields are disabled, select a brush face or whole brush first.

sections.title: Keep texture placement during geometry edits

steps.title: Choose texture lock
steps.text: Enable Texture lock to keep coordinates attached while moving, rotating, or scaling a brush. Some vertex edits need it off because the new shape cannot preserve all UVs.

steps.title: Caulk hidden faces
steps.text: Select opaque brushes and click Auto Caulk to apply caulk to fully covered coplanar faces. Partially exposed faces stay unchanged.

tips: Use Undo if a projection command or Auto Caulk affected an unintended selected surface.
